about: Numbers the ordinary-crime case flow, firearm laws, oversight and fire service use (src/core2/public-safety.ts). Each is tagged SOURCED, ESTIMATED (with source and spread) or TUNABLE (with the spread it is checked against).

daysPerMonth.citation: A billing month of jail days.

reportedRobbery.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json. Robbery 73.4 percent reported.

reportedAssault.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
reportedAssault.estimatedFrom: Aggravated assault 4.7 per 1,000 at 69.1 percent reported and simple assault 14.4 per 1,000 at 40.4 percent, weighted by rate.

spread.citation: The simple and aggravated assault reporting rates.

reportedBurglary.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
reportedBurglary.estimatedFrom: Household burglary is reported about half the time in the NCVS series.

spread.citation: NCVS household property reporting rates across years.

reportedProperty.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
reportedProperty.estimatedFrom: Total household property crime is reported about one time in three in the NCVS series.

spread.citation: NCVS property reporting rates across years.

clearedAssault.citation: FBI, Crime in the United States 2019, Table 25 (percent of offenses cleared by arrest or exceptional means). Aggravated assault 52.3 percent.

clearedRobbery.citation: FBI, Crime in the United States 2019, Table 25 (percent of offenses cleared by arrest or exceptional means). Robbery 30.5 percent.

clearedBurglary.citation: FBI, Crime in the United States 2019, Table 25 (percent of offenses cleared by arrest or exceptional means). Burglary 13.8 percent.

clearedProperty.citation: FBI, Crime in the United States 2019, Table 25 (percent of offenses cleared by arrest or exceptional means). Larceny-theft 17.4 percent.

policeServiceElasticity.citation: How far a police line above or below its base moves clearance: a share of the staffing change reaches the arrest rate.

spread.citation: Checked against the researched police-to-violent-crime link size (-0.34 per unit of officers per 1,000).

serviceFloor.citation: A line cut to a quarter of its base is the lowest service the model reads.

spread.citation: Largest single-year municipal police cuts in the historical record.

serviceCeiling.citation: A line doubled is the highest service the model reads.

spread.citation: Largest single-year municipal police increases in the historical record.

liquidMedianToMean.citation: Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances 2022: median transaction-account balance about $8,000 against a mean near $62,000.
liquidMedianToMean.estimatedFrom: Median over mean of family transaction accounts.

spread.citation: SCF 2019 to 2022 median and mean balances.

dangerDetentionShare.citation: Illinois Pretrial Fairness Act first-year detention petitions (Loyola University Chicago Center for Criminal Justice, 2024): detention petitions were filed in roughly one case in ten and granted in most.
dangerDetentionShare.estimatedFrom: Share of violent-offense adult cases a court detains for danger where money bail has ended.

spread.citation: Loyola first-year report, Cook County against collar counties.

detentionConvictionRatio.citation: Dobbie, Goldin and Yang 2018 (American Economic Review): detained defendants are about 31 percent more likely to be convicted than released ones (data/research/outcome-web/links.json, bail-to-conviction anchor).

convictedShare.assault.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: 66 percent of felony defendants convicted; lower for assault, where charges are dropped more.
convictedShare.assault.estimatedFrom: Share of adult cases ending in conviction across detained and released defendants together.

convictedShare.robbery.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: 66 percent of felony defendants convicted; lower for assault, where charges are dropped more.
convictedShare.robbery.estimatedFrom: Share of adult cases ending in conviction across detained and released defendants together.

convictedShare.burglary.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: 66 percent of felony defendants convicted; lower for assault, where charges are dropped more.
convictedShare.burglary.estimatedFrom: Share of adult cases ending in conviction across detained and released defendants together.

convictedShare.property.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Defendants in Large Urban Counties, 2009: 66 percent of felony defendants convicted; lower for assault, where charges are dropped more.
convictedShare.property.estimatedFrom: Share of adult cases ending in conviction across detained and released defendants together.

dispositionMonths.assault.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, State Court Processing Statistics: median time from arrest to adjudication about three months for felonies.
dispositionMonths.assault.estimatedFrom: Months from arrest to the case's end.

spread.citation: BJS SCPS median days to adjudication by offense.

dispositionMonths.robbery.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, State Court Processing Statistics: median time from arrest to adjudication about three months for felonies.
dispositionMonths.robbery.estimatedFrom: Months from arrest to the case's end.

spread.citation: BJS SCPS median days to adjudication by offense.

dispositionMonths.burglary.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, State Court Processing Statistics: median time from arrest to adjudication about three months for felonies.
dispositionMonths.burglary.estimatedFrom: Months from arrest to the case's end.

spread.citation: BJS SCPS median days to adjudication by offense.

dispositionMonths.property.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, State Court Processing Statistics: median time from arrest to adjudication about three months for felonies.
dispositionMonths.property.estimatedFrom: Months from arrest to the case's end.

spread.citation: BJS SCPS median days to adjudication by offense.

incarceratedShare.assault.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 70 percent of convicted felons got jail or prison.
incarceratedShare.assault.estimatedFrom: Share of convictions sentenced to jail or prison.

prisonShare.assault.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 41 percent of felons to prison, 28 percent to jail.
prisonShare.assault.estimatedFrom: Share of incarcerated sentences served in state prison, the rest in county jail.

incarceratedShare.robbery.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 70 percent of convicted felons got jail or prison.
incarceratedShare.robbery.estimatedFrom: Share of convictions sentenced to jail or prison.

prisonShare.robbery.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 41 percent of felons to prison, 28 percent to jail.
prisonShare.robbery.estimatedFrom: Share of incarcerated sentences served in state prison, the rest in county jail.

incarceratedShare.burglary.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 70 percent of convicted felons got jail or prison.
incarceratedShare.burglary.estimatedFrom: Share of convictions sentenced to jail or prison.

prisonShare.burglary.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 41 percent of felons to prison, 28 percent to jail.
prisonShare.burglary.estimatedFrom: Share of incarcerated sentences served in state prison, the rest in county jail.

incarceratedShare.property.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 70 percent of convicted felons got jail or prison.
incarceratedShare.property.estimatedFrom: Share of convictions sentenced to jail or prison.

prisonShare.property.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: about 41 percent of felons to prison, 28 percent to jail.
prisonShare.property.estimatedFrom: Share of incarcerated sentences served in state prison, the rest in county jail.

jailSentenceDays.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Felony Sentences in State Courts 2006: median jail sentence about six months, served in part; misdemeanor terms shorter.
jailSentenceDays.estimatedFrom: Mean jail days served per jail sentence.

prisonSentenceDays.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Time Served in State Prison, 2018: mean about two years served.
prisonSentenceDays.estimatedFrom: Mean prison days served per prison sentence.

jailPerDiemMinor.citation: Vera Institute of Justice, The Price of Jails, 2015: about $85 a day.
jailPerDiemMinor.estimatedFrom: Average jail cost per inmate day.

prisonPerDiemMinor.citation: Vera Institute of Justice, The Price of Prisons, 2015: $33,274 a year.
prisonPerDiemMinor.estimatedFrom: Average state prison cost per inmate day.

marginalCostShare.citation: Vera Institute of Justice, The Price of Jails, 2015, and CBO: variable cost of one more inmate is a minority of the average cost.
marginalCostShare.estimatedFrom: Share of the per diem that is food, medical and supplies paid to outside vendors for each added jail day; staff and buildings are the corrections line.

courtCostPerCaseMinor.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Indigent Defense Systems and county prosecution budgets: about $1,500 of added defense and prosecution contract cost per adult case.
courtCostPerCaseMinor.estimatedFrom: Marginal county cost of an adult case.

spread.citation: BJS county indigent defense expenditures per case.

juvenileAdjudicatedShare.citation: Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention, Juvenile Court Statistics 2019: about half of petitioned delinquency cases adjudicated.
juvenileAdjudicatedShare.estimatedFrom: Share of juvenile court cases ending in adjudication.

juvenilePlacedShare.citation: OJJDP Juvenile Court Statistics 2019: about 15 percent of adjudicated cases got out-of-home placement.

juvenilePlacementDays.citation: OJJDP Juvenile Residential Facility Census: median length of stay about four months.

juvenilePerDiemMinor.citation: Justice Policy Institute, Sticker Shock 2020: about $588 a day to confine a young person in a state juvenile facility.

juvenileCourtCostPerCaseMinor.citation: County juvenile court and probation costs per petition (OJJDP, Juvenile Court Statistics, and county budgets).
juvenileCourtCostPerCaseMinor.estimatedFrom: Marginal county cost of a juvenile case.

juvenileAgeDefault.citation: National Conference of State Legislatures, Juvenile Age of Jurisdiction 2024: 18 in nearly every state.

juvenileAgeRaised.citation: Vermont Act 201 of 2018 (18-year-olds to juvenile court from 2020, 19-year-olds from 2022); National Conference of State Legislatures, Juvenile Age of Jurisdiction, 2024.

forceClaimShare.citation: Self-defense claims in assault cases (Center for American Progress and state studies of justifiable-force claims).
forceClaimShare.estimatedFrom: Share of assault cases in which the arrested person claims self-defense.

retreatPossibleShare.citation: Duty-to-retreat jurisdictions weigh whether a safe retreat existed; no study counts how often it did.
retreatPossibleShare.estimatedFrom: Share of self-defense claims in which a safe retreat was possible, so the claim fails where the duty to retreat applies.

spread.citation: Spread of cases in the state studies.

storageDeviceMinor.citation: Gun locks run $10 to $100 and safes more; Giffords Law Center and Everytown safe-storage cost surveys.
storageDeviceMinor.estimatedFrom: Mean one-time cost of a lock or lockbox bought to comply.

spread.citation: Retail price range of cable locks, lockboxes and small safes.

permitFeeMinor.citation: State concealed carry permit fees run from about $10 to $200 (Giffords Law Center, Concealed Carry, 2024; state police fee schedules).

permitTrainingMinor.citation: Required live-fire classes cost about $75 to $200 where a state requires training.
permitTrainingMinor.estimatedFrom: Mean training class cost for a first permit.

permitHolderShare.citation: Crime Prevention Research Center, Concealed Carry Permit Holders Across the United States 2023: about 21 million permit holders against about 80 million adult gun owners.
permitHolderShare.estimatedFrom: Share of adults (21 and older) in firearm-owning households who hold a permit where one is required.

permitRampShare.citation: Share of the gap between holders and the target who apply each month after a permit requirement takes effect.

spread.citation: Time for permit counts to settle after Michigan 2001 and Pennsylvania 1989 changes.

permitTermMonths.citation: Most states issue concealed carry permits for four to five years (Giffords Law Center, Concealed Carry, 2024).

handgunPurchaseRate.citation: ATF and NICS data: about 5 million handgun purchases a year among about 80 million gun owners; young adults buy less.
handgunPurchaseRate.estimatedFrom: Yearly share of 18-to-20-year-olds in firearm-owning households who buy a handgun from a private seller where no age limit applies.

handgunPriceMinor.citation: National Shooting Sports Foundation average handgun retail price, about $500.

boardCostPerResidentYearMinor.citation: National Association for Civilian Oversight of Law Enforcement, Oversight Agency Survey 2016: median agency budget near $500,000 in large cities.
boardCostPerResidentYearMinor.estimatedFrom: Yearly board staff and investigation cost per resident of the town.

spread.unit: minor units per resident per year
spread.citation: NACOLE survey, agencies serving 100,000 to 1 million people.

detainerHoldDays.citation: 8 CFR 287.7(d): a detainer asks a jail to hold a person up to 48 hours beyond release.

fireStructureRatePer1000.citation: National Fire Protection Association, Fire Loss in the United States 2022: about 499,000 structure fires against 131 million households.

fireLossMinor.citation: National Fire Protection Association, Fire Loss in the United States 2022: structure fire direct property damage per fire.
fireLossMinor.estimatedFrom: Mean direct property loss per structure fire.

fireUninsuredShare.citation: Insurance Information Institute: about three in ten households lack adequate fire coverage; renters least.
fireUninsuredShare.estimatedFrom: Share of a fire loss the household pays.

spread.citation: III renters and homeowners coverage surveys.

fireServiceLossSlope.citation: How far a fire line above or below its base moves the loss per fire.

spread.citation: NFPA response-time loss studies and ISO class ratings.

youthDeathAgeFrom.citation: America's Health Rankings, Firearm Deaths among Children, ages 1 to 19.

youthDeathAgeBelow.citation: America's Health Rankings, Firearm Deaths among Children, ages 1 to 19.

youthSuicideAgeFrom.citation: Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions, ages 10 to 19.

adultAge.citation: Age of majority in nearly every state.

permitAge.citation: Most permit states issue from age 21 (Giffords Law Center, 2024).

handgunAge.citation: 18 U.S.C. 922(b)(1) and state laws setting 21 for all sales.

childAgeBelow.citation: Child access prevention laws cover minors under 18.

ageProfile.source: FBI, Crime in the United States 2019, Table 38 (arrests by age) against Census population by age: each age band's arrest share over its population share, for violent and property offenses together.
ageProfile.spread: plus or minus 30 percent per band
